## THE FALLBACK IS UP — Gerrit 1311, built under HELD-OUT TDD, and the hold-out earned its keep twice

Change **1311**: `set_parent` writes a non-sub-task's parent as an ordinary update to the
instance-discovered **"Epic Link"** custom field, replacing 1302's refuted `add_issues_to_epic`
route. The dead `agile_rest_path="greenhopper"` option goes with it.

### Method — and it differed from every prior change on this epic

Run under the `/rebar-implement` held-out discipline at the operator's direction, which matters
because this epic has now shipped THREE mutation-proven changes whose feature could not fire (1276,
1288, 1302). The orchestrator authored the full oracle; the **edge and E2E cells were physically
removed from the working tree** — not merely omitted from the prompt, since a subagent can read
files — and a SEPARATE implementation subagent was given ONLY the happy-path cell.

    IN THE TREE (implementer saw):  test_epic_parent_on_a_non_subtask_is_written_as_an_epic_link
    HELD OUT (never saw):           clearing_an_epic_parent_nulls_the_epic_link_field
                                    the_epic_link_field_is_discovered_once_not_per_call
                                    a_client_without_fields_declines_rather_than_raising_attributeerror
                                    an_undiscoverable_epic_link_declines_and_never_writes_fields_parent
                                    subtask_parent_still_uses_fields_parent
                                    the_emit_gate_and_dc_apply_now_overlap

### What the hold-out caught — the part worth recording

First validation against the restored oracle: **2 of the 6 held-out cells FAILED.**

 1. no caching — the field was rediscovered on every `set_parent`, a REST round trip per parent
    write on a reparent-heavy pass (the cost concern b586 already had to address here);
 2. `self._client.fields()` called UNGUARDED — a client without it raised `AttributeError` rather
    than the attributed decline. Not cosmetic: `dispatch_one` classifies by exception type, so
    since 1305 that mis-alerts as the retryable `outbound-parent-failed` instead of the accurate
    `outbound-parent-unrepresentable`.

**Defect 2 is the same mistake I made myself.** Before the operator asked for held-out discipline I
had written this implementation inline, and it had the identical unguarded call — my own six cells
all passed with it present, because every double I wrote has `fields()`. Two independent
implementations fell into the same trap. That is not a fluke; it is a generalization trap that only
a test the implementer could not see was going to catch.

Per the protocol the missing BEHAVIOUR was described to the implementer, not the withheld tests —
so it implemented to a contract rather than over-fitting to an assertion string. Both fixed in one
pass; full oracle then **7/7 GREEN**.

### Teeth — 6 mutations, all killed

    M1  substring match instead of equality ("Epic Name" decoy wins)  -> 4 failed
    M2  drop the per-instance cache                                   -> 1 failed
    M3  drop the getattr capability guard                             -> 1 failed
    M4  clear writes the sentinel "none" instead of JSON null         -> 1 failed
    M5  hardcode customfield_10001 instead of discovering it          -> 5 failed
    M6  never decline (skip the guard)                                -> 2 failed

My first M6 attempt was malformed — it still raised, so it was a no-op that "passed" — and I
re-ran it properly rather than bank a mutation that proved nothing. Refactoring litmus: the cells
assert recorded client calls and exception types, not private names or source text, so a rename or
extraction would not break them.

Gates: ruff clean, mypy 421 files clean, **2132 passed** across
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` + `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler`, transport **781/800**.

### The live cell is REWRITTEN, and this is the part to scrutinise

`test_set_parent_declines_the_epic_case_loudly` asserted the epic case DECLINES — correct while no
fix existed. It is now `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link`: seed a real Epic,
`set_parent` a standard issue under it, read the Epic Link back **over raw REST** (so the write path
and the proving read share no code), then clear and assert the field is null.

This is not an inverted assertion hiding a failure — the expected OUTCOME changed because the
shipped behaviour changed, and the cell still fails if the parent does not land. But it does mean
**5200's row-12 AC now prescribes the wrong mechanism** (it specifies
`pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)` for the epic case). Flagged on 5200 rather than silently
diverging from it.

### STILL UNSETTLED — do not tick AC1 off this

Whether writing the Epic Link custom field actually takes effect on DC 8.17.1 is NOT established.
The unit suite cannot settle it; that is exactly the error 1302 made with 2047 green tests. Only the
next harness run decides, and [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] gives independent reason for caution —
DC may accept-and-ignore parent writes. **Record the run id and whether the field actually held.**
